authors: Geirhos, R., Rubisch, P., Michaelis, C., Bethge, M., Wichmann, F.A. & Brendel, W.
title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are biased towards texture; increasing shape bias improves accuracy and robustness
relevance: Supplies a single hypothesis that unifies both of this project's robustness results, which nothing in the previous 206 rows does: if the U-Net is texture-biased, it should transfer well across sensors whose COLOUR differs wildly but whose texture does not, and it should degrade when RESOLUTION destroys texture. That is exactly the measured pattern - recall within 0.020 across 2005-2021 spanning three providers, but ~6 points worse at 2000/2002 where true GSD is 40 cm against 10 cm. It also predicts why brightness out-performs greenness as a single-pixel cue, and it makes a falsifiable claim we can test by channel ablation rather than by argument.

title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature reliance through controlled suppression
relevance: DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS Geirhos 2019 and therefore contradicts the unifying hypothesis this loop just adopted, which is why it is worth more than a confirming citation. It argues the texture-bias conclusion is an artefact of how the cue-conflict stimuli suppress information, and that controlled suppression gives a different answer. If it is right, our resolution-versus-sensor asymmetry needs a different explanation and a channel-ablation test would be interpreted differently. It should be read BEFORE any design decision is justified by texture bias, not after.

title: Promoting Shape Bias in CNNs: Frequency-Based and Contrastive Regularization for Corruption Robustness
relevance: If the texture-bias reading survives, this is the actionable follow-on: frequency-based regularization to push a CNN toward shape, with corruption robustness as the stated target. Our cross-sensor problem is a corruption-robustness problem in all but name - the same ground rendered by different optics, compression and colour pipelines - and unlike Stylized-ImageNet it does not require restyling a training set we do not have. Relevant only conditionally, which is the honest framing given the contradiction above.
